name: Hash Function Assessment
description: Assessment of cryptographic hash function usage including SHA-2 family, SHA-3, and identification of deprecated functions (MD5, SHA-1). Covers evaluation of collision resistance requirements, preimage resistance, hash function selection for specific use cases, and detection of length-extension vulnerabilities.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to hash function assessment

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands hash function properties and why algorithm selection matters
evidence: Can explain collision resistance, preimage resistance, and second-preimage resistance
Understands why MD5 and SHA-1 are deprecated for security-critical uses (SHA-1 is disallowed for signature generation and NIST plans to retire it entirely by 31 December 2030)
Can describe the SHA-2 and SHA-3 families and their output sizes

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Identifies hash function usage and deprecated algorithms under supervision
evidence: Detects use of MD5 or SHA-1 in certificates, signatures, and integrity checks
Identifies hash function usage in code review under guidance
Uses tools to compute and verify hashes for evidence integrity
Documents hash-related findings following lab templates

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently assesses hash function usage for security and appropriateness
evidence: Evaluates hash function selection against the specific security requirements (collision vs preimage resistance)
Identifies length-extension vulnerabilities where Merkle-Damgard hashes (MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-512) are used as naive secret-prefix MACs
Assesses hash function usage in digital signatures, integrity verification, and commitment schemes
Produces findings referencing NIST SP 800-131A or FIPS 180-4 guidance

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles complex hash function assessment; demonstrates practical attack impact
evidence: Demonstrates MD5 collision attacks and their impact on certificate security
Evaluates custom MAC and hash constructions for length-extension and related structural weaknesses
Assesses hash function usage in Merkle trees, blockchain, and commitment schemes
Reviews and mentors junior staff on hash function assessment

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines hash function assessment methodology; recognised authority on hash security
evidence: Authored or maintains the lab's hash function assessment methodology
Published research on hash function vulnerabilities or practical collision attacks
Provides expert guidance on hash function migration strategies (SHA-1 to SHA-2/SHA-3)
Trains teams on hash function internals, attacks, and selection criteria

assessment_methods.description: Audit a system for deprecated hash function usage: identify all instances, assess risk based on context (signature vs checksum vs HMAC), and produce prioritised remediation recommendations
Given an API using SHA-256 for request signing, determine whether it is vulnerable to length-extension attacks and propose a fix
